title: A session that wraps up offers you a fast worktree cleanup
why: Your idea, Oct 25: when a session thinks its work is wrapped, it should offer you a faster worktree cleanup than the scheduled ones.
note: Checked at claude-settings f463787. Cleanup today runs on its own at four points (decision when-a-worktree-may-be-removed): each agent end removes a finished agent's tree after 30 idle minutes; each session end and the daily job remove a merged tree idle 1 hour, an agent tree idle 4 hours, a pushed unmerged tree idle 24 hours. A dirty or unpushed tree is never removed. The fast path already exists: janitor/sweep.py --attended (a person's run, skips the merged and 1-hour idle keeps) and --fast (only trees whose branch is already in main, no fetch); preview by default, --confirm to remove. Gap: no rule tells a session to offer it, so you never hear of it. Unknown: how many worktrees pile up today on the Mac and Windows (count .claude/worktrees per repo and read state/janitor-runs.jsonl). Advisor pick, not ruled: one sentence in the reports rule's home: when a session's last PR has merged and no lane is open, its final report offers the cleanup as one command you can run (c28 pattern): sweep.py --root <repo> --attended --fast, preview then --confirm. No hook, no new code. Your word, Oct 25: you were checking whether it existed; goal 3 already went out without it, so it waits for a later batch.
